chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Yusuf ibn 'Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever fasts, then forgets and eats and drinks, should not break his fast because of his forgetting, for it is sustenance that Allah (Exalted and Mighty) provided for him, so let him complete his fast.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.فَلَا يُفْطِرُ: So he does not break his fast
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ: So let him complete his fast

ai.seo_question: Does eating or drinking due to forgetfulness break the fast in Islam?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetful eating during Ramadan does not invalidate the fast, as it is viewed as divine sustenance (*rizq*) rather than a deliberate act of breaking the fast. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*yusr*) in worship, distinguishing between intentional nullification and accidental consumption, thereby relieing the believer from the burden of making up the day or offering expiation.
